workingTitle: Webb found an unexpectedly clear sightline through cosmic reionization
topic: Cosmology & Early Universe / Galaxies & Galactic Evolution
coreFacts: JWST/NIRSpec detected flux blueward of Lyman-alpha at about 7 sigma from JADES-GS-z7-LAF at redshift 7.57.
Independent JWST/NIRCam F090W imaging detected the same blueward flux at about 10 sigma.
The flux position is consistent with the galaxy and appears about 0.4 physical kiloparsec from its ultraviolet centroid.
Transmission requires a neutral-hydrogen fraction below 0.00001 in the transmitting parts of this sightline.
The sightline overlaps several high-redshift galaxy overdensities that may help explain the ionized route.
caveats: The work is an unreviewed preprint based on one sightline.
No evidence was found for a foreground interloper, but one cannot be formally excluded.
Low-resolution spectroscopy cannot establish that the entire path was continuously transparent.
The non-ionizing ultraviolet detection does not directly measure the galaxy's ionizing-photon escape fraction.

sources.label: Helton et al., Discovery of the Lyman-alpha Forest in a Star-Forming Galaxy at z approximately 7.57

sourceStatus: Primary preprint abstract and full text verified. A secondary source was unnecessary because the primary source directly supports the material claims.
